title: Northwind Analytics  security review follow-up
next_steps: Redwood to send link to API key rotation/revocation guide
Northwind to rotate keys for all background workers and confirm 401 behavior on revoked key
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 4:00pm PT
Duration: 33 minutes
Attendees: Vanessa Ortiz (Redwood), Dev Patel (Redwood), Morgan Ellis (Northwind), Priya Desai (Northwind)

Summary
Northwind asked about best practice for Hosted API key rotation and what to expect when revoking a key after suspected exposure. Redwood explained the overlap strategy for planned rotations and the revoke-first approach for suspected compromise.

Transcript
[00:00] Vanessa Ortiz: Hey Morgan, Priya  thanks for jumping on. I saw the note about a key potentially showing up in CI logs.
[00:18] Morgan Ellis: Yeah. Were not 100% sure, but we want to be safe. Whats the cleanest way to rotate it, and does revocation take effect immediately?
[00:35] Dev Patel: For suspected exposure, the conservative thing is revoke/disable first, then create a new key and deploy that. For a planned rotation, you can do a two-key overlap: create new, deploy, validate traffic, then revoke the old.
[01:05] Priya Desai: When you say revoke, is that in the console?
[01:10] Vanessa Ortiz: Yep  Console  Settings  API Keys. Theres a disable action. We also have an API endpoint for revoke if you automate it.
[01:28] Morgan Ellis: And after disable, we should see 401s?
[01:33] Dev Patel: Correct. It should be immediate. Rarely theres some edge propagation and you might see a short window, like under a minute, but generally it flips fast.
[02:02] Priya Desai: We have a bunch of workers. So we should make sure all of them pick up the new secret, otherwise intermittent 401s?
[02:10] Vanessa Ortiz: Exactly. Thats the most common issue  one background job still using the old key.
[02:25] Morgan Ellis: Can you send the doc?
[02:28] Vanessa Ortiz: Yep, Ill send the rotation/revocation guide right after this. Also just a reminder  please dont paste key values into tickets or email. We can work off names/IDs.
[03:10] Morgan Ellis: Sounds good.
[30:55] Vanessa Ortiz: Cool. Next steps: well send the guide, youll rotate across the workers and confirm behavior. If anything weird, send request IDs and timestamps.
[31:12] Morgan Ellis: Will do. Thanks.
